title: Review model prefix can't resolve
body:
`OPENCODE_REVIEW_MODEL: "miaou/glm-5"` is passed to `opencode run --model`, which opencode resolves as `provider_id/model_id`. The only provider declared anywhere in this repo is `camer-digital` (.opencode/opencode.json:13; auth.placeholder.json keys on `camer-digital`), and `miaou` is not a builtin opencode provider. So unless `OPENCODE_REVIEW_MODEL` is overridden in GitLab project CI settings (not visible from the repo), the default `opencode-review` job hits `ProviderModelNotFoundError` and the review silently never runs — masked by `allow_failure: true`. Fix: set it to `camer-digital/glm-5` to match the declared provider.

**Evidence:** .gitlab-ci.yml:9 `OPENCODE_REVIEW_MODEL: "miaou/glm-5"`; .opencode/opencode.json:12-13 declares provider `camer-digital` only, with model `glm-5` in nameOverrides (opencode.json:27); auth.placeholder.json keys on `camer-digital`; no `miaou` provider declaration anywhere in repo (semantic search returned only unrelated secrets files).

title: BouncyCastle jdk25on artifacts don't exist on Maven Central
body:
The `jdk18on` suffix on BouncyCastle artifacts means "Java 1.8 **and later**" — `bcprov-jdk18on` / `bcpkix-jdk18on` already run perfectly on Java 25; there is no separate `jdk25on` artifact line. The Maven Central directory listing (`repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/bouncycastle/`) enumerates `bc-jdk14-bom`, `bc-jdk15to18-bom`, `bc-jdk18on-bom`, `bc-lts8on-bom` — no `jdk25on` directory — and BouncyCastle's own docs confirm the standard naming is `<module>-jdk18on-<version>`. Version 1.84 (the pinned version) is confirmed to ship only `jdk18on` artifacts. A search for "bcprov-jdk25on" / "bcpkix-jdk25on" returns zero results. If these artifacts cannot be resolved from Central, the build fails. Fix: revert both the property and the two dependency declarations back to `bcpkix-jdk18on` / `bcprov-jdk18on` (keep `${...version}` = 1.84 or bump to 1.85).

**Evidence:** pom.xml:160 `<bcpkix-jdk25on.version>1.84</bcpkix-jdk25on.version>`; pom.xml:687 `<artifactId>bcpkix-jdk25on</artifactId>`; pom.xml:693 `<artifactId>bcprov-jdk25on</artifactId>`. Maven Central directory (repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/bouncycastle/) lists no jdk25on artifacts; BC docs confirm naming convention is -jdk18on (Java 8+). Version 1.84 confirmed to ship jdk18on only.

title: Gateway route property prefix not updated for new starter
body:
The new `spring-cloud-starter-gateway-server-webflux` (Spring Cloud 2025.1 / Gateway 5.x) remapped the route property namespace from `spring.cloud.gateway.routes[...]` to `spring.cloud.gateway.server.webflux.routes[...]` (confirmed by Spring Cloud Gateway docs: https://docs.spring.io/spring-cloud-gateway/reference/spring-cloud-gateway-server-webflux/configuration.html). The proxy-server's `src/main/resources/application.properties` still defines all 9 production routes with the legacy prefix (`spring.cloud.gateway.routes[0].id = consents`, etc.). With the new starter, these properties are silently ignored — the proxy-server will register zero routes and forward nothing. The programmatic `RouteLocator` in `ApplicationProxyWireMockTest` still works (Java API is namespace-independent), so CI doesn't catch this. Fix: update every `spring.cloud.gateway.routes` key in `application.properties` to `spring.cloud.gateway.server.webflux.routes`.

**Evidence:** proxy-server/pom.xml:57 `<artifactId>spring-cloud-starter-gateway-server-webflux</artifactId>`; proxy-server/src/main/resources/application.properties uses `spring.cloud.gateway.routes[0].id = consents` (and [1]..[8]). Spring Cloud Gateway server-webflux docs show routes under `spring.cloud.gateway.server.webflux.routes`. SO answer: "route configuration for the reactive stack must now be defined under spring.cloud.gateway.server.webflux.routes".

title: Disabled test masks the route regression
body:
This test — the integration test that verifies the proxy forwards requests (expecting "Connection refused" = route found, backend down) — is disabled with "Spring Cloud / Boot compatibility issues." It is exactly the test that would fail when the legacy `spring.cloud.gateway.routes` properties are silently ignored by the new gateway starter (see the pom.xml finding). Disabling it masks the route-registration regression. Re-enable it after fixing the property namespace; if other issues remain, file a separate issue rather than leaving a test permanently `@Disabled`.

**Evidence:** ApplicationProxyTest.java line 22: `@org.junit.jupiter.api.Disabled("Disabled temporarily: Spring Cloud / Boot compatibility issues")` — test verifies proxy routing via WebTestClient expecting "Connection refused" error.

title: Review model id prefix can't resolve
body:
`OPENCODE_REVIEW_MODEL: "miaou/glm-5"` cannot resolve: opencode resolves `--model` as `provider_id/model_id`, but `.opencode/opencode.json` declares only a provider keyed `camer-digital` (with model ids `glm-5`, `kimi-k2-instruct`, etc.). `miaou` appears nowhere as a provider key — not in the config, not in `auth.placeholder.json`, not in the repo. So the default `opencode-review` job will fail to find the model and exit non-zero, which `allow_failure: true` silently swallows — the review feature is effectively dead unless an operator overrides `OPENCODE_REVIEW_MODEL` in CI settings. Fix: set it to `camer-digital/glm-5`.

**Evidence:** .gitlab-ci.yml:9 — OPENCODE_REVIEW_MODEL: "miaou/glm-5"; .opencode/opencode.json provider block keyed "camer-digital" with model ids glm-5/kimi-k2-instruct/deepseek-v3p2/minimax-m2p5; no "miaou" provider declared anywhere.

title: curl|bash from mutable GitHub main
body:
The before_script pipes `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/upciti/wakemeops/main/assets/install_repository` directly into `bash`. This fetches from the mutable `main` branch with no checksum/pin, so any compromise or accidental push to that branch runs arbitrary code in the review job. Pin to a release tag or commit SHA, or vendor the install script into the repo. Low severity because this is a CI helper installer in a non-blocking job, but it is a supply-chain vector.

**Evidence:** .gitlab-ci.yml:33 — curl --silent --show-error --location "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/upciti/wakemeops/main/assets/install_repository" | bash

title: OIDC client creds not declared in CI
body:
`opencode.json` reads `{env:OIDC_CLIENT_ID}` and `{env:OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET}`, but `.gitlab-ci.yml` only declares `OIDC_ISSUER` and `OIDC_SCOPE` — the client-id/secret are neither in the YAML nor documented. In the default Mode A (`OPENCODE_USE_EXPLICIT_TOKEN: "false"`) the oauth2 plugin needs both at request time; if they are not set as masked CI/CD variables in the GitLab project settings, the provider cannot authenticate and the review job silently fails behind `allow_failure: true`. Either declare them (as protected/masked project variables) or add a comment documenting where they must be set.

**Evidence:** .opencode/opencode.json:19-20 — "clientId": "{env:OIDC_CLIENT_ID}", "clientSecret": "{env:OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET}"; .gitlab-ci.yml:11-12 only define OIDC_ISSUER and OIDC_SCOPE.

title: get-token.sh referenced but absent
body:
When `OPENCODE_USE_EXPLICIT_TOKEN` is `"true"`, the before_script runs `sh "${CI_PROJECT_DIR}/scripts/get-token.sh"`, but that script is not present in the repo (`read_file` confirms it does not exist) and is not added by this diff. Flipping the flag to `true` would break the job immediately. This path is off by default (`"false"`), so it is non-blocking, but either add the script or remove the dead reference to avoid a future footgun.

**Evidence:** .gitlab-ci.yml:46 — sh "${CI_PROJECT_DIR}/scripts/get-token.sh"; scripts/get-token.sh not found in repo (read_file returns "file not found").
